title: Mixed-ring chain currying and descent naturality
statement:
Let $S\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $U$ restriction of scalars. Use integer-indexed cochain complexes and derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], product total Hom with differential $d(f)=d_Nf-(-1)^nf d$ [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], and direct-sum total tensor with differential $d(a\otimes t)=da\otimes t+(-1)^pa\otimes dt$ for $a\in A^p$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For arbitrary $B$-complexes $A,T$ and $S$-complex $N$, put $J(T,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(UT,N)$ with $(bh)(t)=h(bt)$. There is a natural isomorphism of entire $S$-complexes
$$\theta_{A,T,N}:U\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(A,J(T,N))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(U\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_B T),N),\qquad \theta(f)(a\otimes t)=f(a)(t),$$
with inverse $g\mapsto(a\mapsto(t\mapsto g(a\otimes t)))$. These formulas are balanced and inverse for the products indexed by all degree pairs, without boundedness assumptions. In degree $n$, both $d(\theta f)$ and $\theta(df)$ evaluate at $a\otimes t$, $a\in A^p$, to
$$d_Nf(a)(t)-(-1)^{p+n}f(a)(d_Tt)-(-1)^nf(d_Aa)(t).$$
For chain maps $\alpha:A'\to A$, $\beta:T'\to T$ and $\gamma:N\to N'$, the square with left vertical map $f\mapsto(a'\mapsto\gamma\circ f(\alpha a')\circ\beta)$ and right vertical map $g\mapsto\gamma\circ g\circ U(\alpha\otimes\beta)$ commutes. If $T,T'$ are K-flat over $B$ [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], $N,N'$ are K-injective over $S$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ are quasi-isomorphisms, these vertical maps are quasi-isomorphisms. On these resolved models the localized squares commute for arbitrary chain maps and for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. The localized family is independent of the chosen resolved representatives and natural for arbitrary morphisms of their represented derived objects, contravariantly in $[A],[T]$ and covariantly in $[N]$, under the canonical tensor and Hom model identifications. No assertion that restriction preserves K-injectives is made.

source.place: Tag 09LN (lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction), differential graded clause and omitted-proof hint; naturality and localization on K-flat/K-injective models are the explicit mixed-ring adaptation.

proof.text: Give $J(T,N)$ the stated $B$-action. Since $d_T(bt)=b\,d_Tt$, the Hom differential satisfies $d(bh)(t)=d_Nh(bt)-(-1)^{|h|}h(bd_Tt)=(b\,dh)(t)$. Also $b(ch)(t)=h(cb t)=((bc)h)(t)$ and $1h=h$. For fixed degrees $p,q,n$, a $B$-linear map $A^p\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(T^q,N^{p+q+n})$ gives the additive, $S$-bilinear pairing $\psi(a,t)=f(a)(t)$ with $\psi(ba,t)=f(a)(bt)=\psi(a,bt)$. Hence it respects the additive and balancing relations defining $A^p\otimes_B T^q$, and defines an $S$-linear map from that tensor product. Conversely an $S$-linear map from this tensor product gives $S$-linear maps in $t$ and is $B$-linear in $a$ for the precomposition action. Evaluation shows that these two operations are inverse.

source.place: Tag 09LN, lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, differential graded clause and bilinear-map hint; explicit commutative mixed-ring specialization.

proof.text: A degree-$n$ cochain on the left is exactly a family $f_{p,q}:A^p\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(T^q,N^{p+q+n})$ for all $(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2$: a map into a product is the family of its component maps. Apply Step 1 to every pair. A map from $\bigoplus_{p+q=k}A^p\otimes_B T^q$ to $N^{k+n}$ is precisely a family of maps on its summands. Finally $(k,p,q)$ with $p+q=k$ is reindexed by $(p,q)$. This identifies both degree-$n$ terms with the same product of $S$-modules, without commuting a product with a tensor product or imposing finite support on cochains. Only elements of the tensor direct sum have finite support. The componentwise inverse is the formula in the statement, and all maps are $S$-linear.

source.place: Tag 09LN, lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, differential graded clause and bilinear-map hint; explicit commutative mixed-ring specialization.

proof.text: Let $|f|=n$, $|a|=p$, and $|t|=q$. Expanding the two Hom differentials gives $(df)(a)(t)=d_Nf(a)(t)-(-1)^{p+n}f(a)(d_Tt)-(-1)^nf(d_Aa)(t)$: the inner cochain $f(a)$ has degree $p+n$. On the other side, $d(\theta f)(a\otimes t)=d_Nf(a)(t)-(-1)^n\{f(d_Aa)(t)+(-1)^pf(a)(d_Tt)\}$. Since $(-1)^n(-1)^p=(-1)^{p+n}$, these agree. Equality on every pure tensor and every summand proves equality of the entire degree maps. Thus the inverse degreewise maps of Step 2 commute with differentials and form the asserted chain isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09LN, lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, differential graded clause and bilinear-map hint; explicit commutative mixed-ring specialization.

proof.text: For chain maps $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ as in the statement, both routes around the square evaluate on $a'\otimes t'$ to $\gamma(f(\alpha a')(\beta t'))$. This proves the square by the same summandwise equality test; no sign occurs because all three maps have degree zero. Precomposition and postcomposition respect identities and composition by associativity of composition, so these are the three-variable naturality squares, with the stated variances.

source.place: Tag 09LN, lemma-tensor-hom-adjunction, differential graded clause and bilinear-map hint; explicit commutative mixed-ring specialization.

proof.text: Assume now that $T,T'$ are K-flat and $\alpha,\beta$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Factor $\alpha\otimes\beta$ as $A'\otimes T'\xrightarrow{\alpha\otimes1}A\otimes T'\xrightarrow{1\otimes\beta}A\otimes T$. The first map is a quasi-isomorphism by the quasi-isomorphism-preservation clause of [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], with fixed K-flat factor $T'$. For the second use [lem-pc-kflat-tensor-quasi-iso] with $R=B$, $E=T'$, $E'=T$, and arbitrary $N=A$. Its order of factors is reversed by the signed flip $a\otimes t\mapsto(-1)^{pq}t\otimes a$ in degrees $(p,q)$. This is an invertible chain map: the two differential terms have respective exponents $(p+1)q$ and $p+p(q+1)$, equal modulo $2$ to $pq+q$ and $pq$ on the flipped side. Thus the second map too is a quasi-isomorphism. Restriction $U$ preserves these quasi-isomorphisms: kernels and images of a $B$-linear differential, and their quotient, have the same underlying additive groups after restriction.

Apply [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] on the small one-object site with ring $S$. Take its source quasi-isomorphism to be $U(\alpha\otimes\beta)$ from Step 5 and its target quasi-isomorphism to be $\gamma:N\to N'$ between K-injective $S$-complexes. It gives exactly the right vertical quasi-isomorphism $g\mapsto\gamma gU(\alpha\otimes\beta)$. The commuting square of Step 4 and the chain isomorphisms of Step 3 identify the left vertical map with the conjugate of this right vertical map, so it also induces isomorphisms on all cohomology groups. The hypothesis on K-injectivity is used only over $S$. Applying the same cited lemma to $U\beta:UT'\to UT$ and $\gamma$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $J(T,N)\to J(T',N')$. It is $B$-linear since $\beta(bt')=b\beta(t')$; restriction to $S$ detects quasi-isomorphisms by the same kernel/image calculation. These are the canonical $J$ comparisons on the left.

source.place: Tag 0A95, lemma-RHom-well-defined, on the one-object ringed site.

proof.text: For later identification of the left model, $J(T,N)$ is K-injective over $B$ when $T$ is K-flat over $B$ and $N$ is K-injective over $S$. Indeed, for an acyclic $B$-complex $F$, $F\otimes_B T$ is acyclic by [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], and remains acyclic after $U$. Apply [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] over $S$ to $0\to U(F\otimes_B T)$ and $1_N$: its Hom complex is acyclic. Step 3 identifies this with the underlying $S$-complex of $\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(F,J(T,N))$. By [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-homotopy] on the one-object $B$-site, its $H^0$ is the group of $B$-linear chain maps $F\to J(T,N)$ modulo $B$-linear homotopy. This group is zero. Thus every such map is null-homotopic, exactly [def-pur-kinjective-complex].

source.place: Tag 0A95, lemma-RHom-well-defined, and Tag 0A8Z, equation-global-cohomology-hom-complex; combined with the chain currying calculation above.

proof.text: The natural squares also pass to homotopy classes. Apply [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy] to $\operatorname{Mod}(B)$: it supplies tensor on the homotopy category; the tensor of modules is additive and preserves direct sums in both variables. Apply [lem-sf-equivariant-hom-resolution-calculus] to $H=\operatorname{Hom}_S(-,-)$ on $S$-modules. Its source homotopy formula is $f\mapsto(-1)^nfh$ on degree $n$, and its target formula is $f\mapsto h'f$. These show that the right-hand Hom construction respects homotopies of all three maps. Restriction just forgets part of the scalar action and preserves the equations defining a homotopy. Step 4, conjugated by $\theta$, gives the same conclusion for the left side, so $\theta$ is a natural isomorphism already on the homotopy-category models.

source.place: Tag 064I, lemma-derived-tor-homotopy, and Tag 0GWP, lemma-symmetric-monoidal-homotopy-category; Hom homotopies as in sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 0A8X.

proof.text: Here are the resolving categories used for descent. The $A$ variable ranges over $K(B)$, whose quasi-isomorphism localization is $D(B)$. For $T$ first use the full homotopy subcategory $\mathcal P$ of flat-term K-flat complexes: [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] on the one-object $B$-site says $W^{-1}\mathcal P\simeq D(B)$, where $W$ consists of its quasi-isomorphisms. For $N$ use the full homotopy subcategory $\mathcal I$ of K-injective $S$-complexes: [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives full faithfulness into $D(S)$ and [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] gives essential surjectivity on the small one-object $S$-site, so $\mathcal I\simeq D(S)$. These statements have no boundedness requirement. Every K-flat $T$ lacking flat terms receives a quasi-isomorphism $P\to T$ from a flat-term K-flat $P$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution].

source.place: Tags 06YS and 06YU, lemma-K-flat-resolution and definition-derived-tor with its preceding construction; Tag 07A5, section-unbounded. Also derived.tex, Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective.

proof.text: Localize the values of the two functors of Step 8 in $D(S)$. By Step 6 they invert quasi-isomorphisms in each variable (take the other two maps to be identities). Apply the functor and natural-transformation clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] successively in $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $T^{\mathrm{op}}$, and use the equivalence $\mathcal I\simeq D(S)$ of Step 9 in $N$. Uniqueness in that universal property makes the successive descents compatible and gives one natural isomorphism on $D(B)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(B)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(S)$. For a quasi-isomorphism square $R\theta=\theta'L$, both vertical arrows become invertible by Step 6, and multiplication gives $R^{-1}\theta'=\theta L^{-1}$: this is the square for its inverse. Identity and composition then give the squares for every localized morphism. For an arbitrary K-flat $T$, use $P\to T$ from Step 9 and Step 6 to identify its component with that on $P$. Naturality for this map and uniqueness of descent make that identification independent of $P$ and compatible with any third representative.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization, and natural-transformation descent by the functor-category universal property; applied to the resolving localizations of Step 9.

proof.text: These are the canonical model identifications in the statement. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to A$. Tensoring it with K-flat $T$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. If also $Q\to T$ is a flat-term K-flat resolution, [lem-pc-kflat-tensor-quasi-iso] identifies $P\otimes_B Q$ with $P\otimes_B T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $P\otimes_B Q$ is the two-resolved model of $[A]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}[T]$ and its comparisons are natural and compatible with inversion. Thus $A\otimes_B T$ is its one-resolved model. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], the right Hom is a model of $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(U([A]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}[T]),[N])$, since $N$ is K-injective. The same definition over $B$, together with Step 7, identifies the left Hom with $U R\operatorname{Hom}_B([A],[J(T,N)])$. Step 10 and uniqueness of localization comparisons make these identifications independent of representatives and natural for arbitrary derived morphisms. Throughout, restriction has been used for exactness and homotopy equations, never to preserve K-injectivity.
